business_problem: DKV Mobility needed to replace batch ETL and Kafka operations overhead so fuel-card and mobility customers could see pricing and transaction data in near real time while the company migrated to Azure and scaled microservices.
solution_summary: DKV Mobility moved its customer-facing mobility platform from self-managed Kafka and batch ETL toward Confluent Cloud so product teams could deliver real-time services without carrying infrastructure operations. The streaming backbone supports fuel-card, EV charging, toll, and transaction use cases that had relied on a legacy ERP process and delayed updates. During the rollout, Confluent consultants helped the platform team migrate workloads, continue the move from private cloud to Azure, and integrate data across departments using JDBC Source and Sink Connectors, the AzureDataLake2 Sink Connector, the HTTP Sink Connector, and Schema Registry. Kafka Streams powers real-time processing on top of those flows. The result is a self-service platform where teams can provision clusters and topics in minutes, push pricing and transaction data to portals and mobile apps, and keep billions of third-party transactions flowing with zero downtime during the cloud migration.

solution_components.name: Confluent Cloud
solution_components.role: Runs the managed streaming backbone for DKV Mobility's customer-facing mobility applications.

solution_components.name: JDBC Source and Sink Connectors
solution_components.role: Integrate operational systems and databases with the streaming platform.

solution_components.name: AzureDataLake2 Sink Connector
solution_components.role: Delivers streaming data into DKV Mobility's Azure-based data lake environment.

solution_components.name: HTTP Sink Connector
solution_components.role: Pushes streaming outputs into downstream HTTP-based services.

solution_components.name: Schema Registry
solution_components.role: Manages schemas across clusters and teams during migration and CI/CD-driven changes.

solution_components.name: Kafka Streams
solution_components.role: Lets developers implement real-time stream processing without owning low-level failure handling.

data_flow: Transaction, pricing, and third-party mobility data flow from ERP and other platforms into Confluent Cloud through JDBC and HTTP connectors, are processed with Kafka Streams, land in Azure data lake targets, and then power portals, apps, and authorization flows in near real time.
business_outcome: DKV Mobility reduced platform operations work, kept production streaming online through its Azure migration, accelerated self-service for developers, and gave fleets fresh pricing and transaction visibility in minutes or seconds instead of hours or weeks.
architecture_clues: The platform team provisioned clusters for eight product teams in minutes.
Schema Registry, RBAC, and ACLs support CI/CD-driven evolution of the streaming platform.
Confluent Connectors simplified cross-department data exchange during the private-cloud-to-Azure migration.
evidence_quotes: Additionally, the DKV Mobility portal could take up to three weeks to ingest transaction data via a legacy enterprise resource planning (ERP) system.
Customers could access those insights in minutes or even seconds.

Confluent Connectors - including the JDBC Source and Sink Connectors, the AzureDataLake2 Sink Connector, and the HTTP Sink Connector - simplified the exchange of data between departments across the organization.
Before adopting Confluent Cloud, platform team members spent close to 10% of their time (around eight hours per week) managing Kafka clusters.
